function: GPT-2 with LoRA predicts future UAV range and angle (CSI) from history echoes; PD-Net maps predicted CSI to sum-rate-maximizing beamformers (pp. 6-8).
system: ISAC-BS with 10 transmit and 10 receive antennas, frequency diverse array, 2 single-antenna UAVs, f0=10 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 8).
method: Supervised LoRA fine-tuning of pre-trained GPT-2 (NMSE loss) for prediction; PD-Net: two feed-forward networks trained with unsupervised adversarial primal-dual loss, no labels (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Own simulator: LoS path-loss and steering-vector channels, UAVs on uniform linear tracks, MUSIC estimates as targets; 22000 training samples; no 3GPP or measured data (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Training: 22000 samples, UAV velocity uniform 5-25 m/s; testing: 5 velocities from 5 to 25 m/s, 1000 samples each; prediction steps 1-5 (p. 8).
baselines: Channel prediction: Transformer, LSTM, GRU (learned); beamforming: SCA (non-learned), PFNN penalty-based FNN (learned) (pp. 9-11).
metrics: NMSE of channel prediction versus velocity and prediction step; average achievable rate versus transmit power and antennas; parameters, training and inference times (pp. 9-12).
complexity: LLM O(N_L q^2 d_LLM + N_L q d_LLM^2); PD-Net inference O(4KN_t F_h + F F_h^2); parameters and per-batch times in Tables V-VI (pp. 7, 8, 10, 12).
q1_support: p. 3: "where L0 refers to the path-loss at the reference distance of" 1 meter. The channel is a custom LoS path-loss and steering-vector model; the paper names no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "set includes 5 velocities ranging from 5 m/s to 25 m/s,". The test velocities lie inside the uniform 5-25 m/s training range of the same simulator; no train-test mismatch of scenario, antennas or frequency is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "In addition, the PD-Net outperforms the PFNN". SCA is the non-learned baseline (p. 10) and PFNN the learned one; the LLM is compared with Transformer, LSTM and GRU (p. 9), on rate (Figs. 12, 13) and NMSE (Figs. 7, 8).
q4_support: p. 7: "its approximate inference computational complexity is dominated by the backbone", O(N_L q^2 d_LLM + N_L q d_LLM^2); p. 8 gives PD-Net orders (Eqs. 34, 35), and Tables V and VI (pp. 10, 12) give parameters and times.
q5_support: p. 8: "proposed NNs are implemented in Python 3.8.20 with Pytorch". No code or data link appears anywhere; the 22000 training samples are simulated and not released, and no public dataset is used.
notes: Title on page 1 is Large Language Model-Enabled Sensing-Aided Communication and the DOI matches. Area 5 by the precedence order: stage 1 (LLM channel prediction from echoes) would be area 2 and stage 2 (PD-Net beamforming) is beamforming in an ISAC system; the paper frames itself as ISAC. The PD-Net objective is communication sum rate only, so a reviewer may prefer area 2 or 3. ris is 0 because Table I (p. 2) marks this work without IRS. Tables I, III-VII and Figs. 7, 8, 12, 13 were read on pages 2 and 8-12 of the PDF image.
